intro.h1: Plan your Wi-Fi mesh on your floor plan
intro.p: Planejador WiFi shows where the signal reaches before you buy a router: draw the walls, place the router and mesh nodes, and see the coverage on 2.4, 5 and 6 GHz. Free, no sign-up, and your projects stay in your browser.

guide.howToSteps:
• Click New project and enter the width and depth of the lot or the house.
  • If you have the floor plan as a photo or an image, load it under File › Plan and scale and set the scale with Measure.
  • With the Wall tool, draw the outer and inner walls and pick the material. Doors and windows are walls too, made of wood or glass.
  • With Router, place the main router where the ISP modem is, then the other nodes.
  • Switch between 2.4, 5 and 6 GHz and look at the heat map. Green is excellent signal; red is no usable signal.
  • Use Suggest a spot to find where one more node helps most, and File › Export JSON to keep the project.
guide.wallsTitle: How much each wall takes from the signal
guide.wallsText: Every wall the signal crosses adds a loss in decibels (dB). Each 10 dB cuts the received power to one tenth, so two or three brick walls already make a difference. The values below are the averages the planner uses; real loss depends on thickness, moisture and steel reinforcement.
guide.signalText: Wi-Fi signal is measured in dBm and is always negative: the closer to zero, the better.
guide.signalRows: −60 dBm or betterExcellent4K streaming, online gaming and the full speed of your plan.−60 to −67 dBmGoodStable HD video and video calls. The target for rooms you use.−67 to −72 dBmFairBrowsing and messaging work; video may stutter.−72 to −80 dBmWeakSlow and unstable.below −80 dBmNo usable signalThe connection drops often.
guide.bandsText:
2.4 GHz reaches farther and goes through walls better, but it is slow and shared with your neighbors. Good for smart-home devices and far corners.

5 GHz is the everyday balance: much faster, with medium range. Check the map on this band first.

6 GHz, found on Wi-Fi 6E and tri-band Wi-Fi 7 routers, is the fastest and least crowded, but loses more at every wall. It shines in the router's own room and on the link between mesh nodes.

faq.a: It is an estimate with a typical error of 8 dB either way. Use it to compare placements and decide how many nodes to buy. After installing, confirm with a Wi-Fi analyzer app on your phone.

faq.q: How many mesh nodes do I need?
faq.a: As a rule of thumb, one node per 80 to 120 m² (860 to 1,300 sq ft) in a brick house, and one per floor in multi-story homes. Concrete walls, slabs and long houses need more. Draw your plan and use Suggest a spot to see whether another node pays off.

faq.q: Where should I put the main router?
faq.a: As close to the center of the house as possible, about 1 meter (3 ft) off the floor, away from fridges, mirrors and metal cabinets. If the modem sits in a corner, run a network cable to a central spot or put a mesh node there.

faq.q: Is a Wi-Fi 7 mesh with 6 GHz worth it?
faq.a: The 6 GHz band is fast and uncrowded but goes through walls poorly. It is most useful for the link between nodes and for devices in the same room. For internet plans up to 1 Gbps, a dual-band Wi-Fi 7 mesh is usually enough.
Wired whenever you can: speed does not drop and nodes can sit farther apart. Wirelessly, aim for −60 to −70 dBm between nodes. Below that, devices connected to the far node get much slower.
Only in your browser, in the device's local storage. Nothing is sent to a server. To keep a copy or open it on another computer, use File and then Export JSON.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy | Planejador WiFi
privacy.description: How Planejador WiFi handles your data: projects are stored only in your browser.
privacy.projectsText: The floor plans, routers and models you create are stored only in your browser's local storage (localStorage). They are not sent to any server. If you clear your browser data, they are gone; to keep a copy, use File › Export JSON.
privacy.noCookies: This site uses no cookies and no third-party tracking tools.
privacy.rightsText: You can ask for information about how your data is processed, or for its deletion, at contato@planejadorwifi.com.

hints.select: Click a wall, node or link to edit it. Drag nodes and names to move them, or the background to move the plan. Ctrl + scroll zooms.
hints.wall: Click and drag to draw a wall. Ends snap to the 25 cm grid and to existing walls. For angled walls, untick “Lock to 90°”.
hints.node: Click where the modem is to place the main router, then where each mesh node goes.
hints.label: Click on the plan and type the room name. Enter confirms.
hints.measure: Drag to measure a distance. With a background image, use this to set the scale.
hints.erase: Click a wall, node or name to delete it.

readout.idle: Hover over the plan to read the signal.
readout.idleTouch: Tap the plan to read the signal.

floors.removeMsg: The walls, nodes and names on this floor will be deleted.

panel.linksHint: Each row shows which node each one connects to (Node 2 → Router). Wirelessly, aim for −60 to −70 dBm; below that, connect them with a network cable.

panel.suggestResult: A {model} at the marked spot (x {x}, y {y} m) takes {band} coverage from {from} to {to}.
panel.suggestRelaxed: No useful spot has a good wireless link to the other nodes: connect this one with a cable.

steps.title: Welcome to Planejador WiFi
steps.body: In under a minute: draw your house, place the router and see where Wi-Fi reaches well. Everything stays in your browser.

steps.title: Your projects
steps.body: Start a New project for your home. The example house stays saved for reference. Under File you export and import projects as JSON.

steps.title: Draw the walls
steps.body: Drag on the map to draw. The material is in the tool options: brick, concrete, glass… Doors and windows are walls too.

steps.title: Place the router
steps.body: Mark where the modem is: the main router goes there. Then add the mesh nodes and check the link between them.

steps.title: Compare the bands
steps.body: Switch between 2.4, 5 and 6 GHz. Green is excellent signal; red is no usable signal.

steps.title: See the result
steps.body: The plan in short: how many devices, whether one needs a cable, and the coverage on each band.

steps.title: Ask for a suggestion
steps.body: Suggest a spot tests every free point and shows where one more node helps most.
